subject: fix(web): settle idle sessions, and pin the delta/final duplicate to its real cause
instruction:
fix(web): settle idle sessions, and pin the delta/final duplicate to its real cause

Two defects from the first live browser pass.

IDLE TRIAGE — fixed. An idle session with no pending approvals now lands in the
third group reading "idle · <age>", and NEEDS YOU is entered by exactly two
doors: an unanswered approval, or status == awaiting_approval. A test enumerates
every status on both planes against both doors rather than sampling, because a
group the page is arranged around is worth exactly as much as the things that
cannot enter it.

This is a DELIBERATE DIVERGENCE from the terminal client, not a port of it:
`SessionInfo::triage` (tui/src/model.rs:249-254) routes interactive+idle to
Triage::NeedsInput and argues for it in a comment. That reasoning does not
survive a rail a person scans for work — every conversation anyone has finished
reading is idle. The divergence is named in `triage_of/2` and in the test, so
nobody later "restores parity" by accident.

DUPLICATE AGENT MESSAGE — diagnosed, not fixed here, because it is not where it
was thought to be. It is not the stream keys: a new test drives deltas, then
provider_event + usage + output_text_final + turn_completed through the fake
plane and asserts the rendered rows equal one project/1 pass over the same
events. They do — same row count, same number of agent messages. The live path
is faithful.

`project/1` itself emits the answer twice. A non-text event flushes the pending
draft into a Message cell; output_text_final then finds no draft to absorb and
pushes a second Message with the same text. `transcript_cells.rs:2056-2086` does
the identical thing, so both surfaces duplicate and the corpus has no fixture for
this interleaving.

The fix belongs in the projection on both sides plus that fixture (docs/WEB.md
§6); changing only the Elixir would make the renderers disagree with nothing
testing the disagreement. Those modules are locked to this slice, so a tripwire
test pins the current output and tells whoever fixes it to assert 1 instead.

Acceptance. These tests are restored into the worktree after the session ends and must pass:
  - a settling turn does not add a stream row the projection did not ask for
  - KNOWN DEFECT: the projection emits a settled answer twice when notes interleave
  - an idle session settles, on either plane, and is never NEEDS YOU
  - but an idle session holding an unanswered approval still needs a person
  - NEEDS YOU has exactly two doors
  - an idle session is drawn in the third group, reading 'idle · <age>'
  - and its age is printed once, not once in the line and again in the column
  - an idle session with an unanswered ask is a card again, with the eye

Rules. Files that already exist under `test/` must not be modified or deleted — the change is graded against tests restored from the history after the session ends, applied to a fresh checkout of the starting commit. New test files of your own are allowed and are left in place, but they are yours: they are not copied into the tree the grade runs in. The change is collected as a diff over `lib/`, `assets/`, `priv/`, `config/`, `docs/` and `README.md`; a change to any other path — `mix.exs` and `.formatter.exs` included — is refused rather than graded. Work only inside this worktree.
